hooks.text: One of the universe's largest black holes has mysteriously vanished.
Where did a supermassive black hole weighing 100 billion suns go?
A colossal galaxy ten times larger than ours has no central heart.

title: The Galaxy With a Missing Heart
description: Astronomers expected one of the largest supermassive black holes in the universe to be lurking inside galaxy A2261-BCG, but they found an empty cosmic ghost town.

beats.text: One of the universe's largest black holes has mysteriously vanished.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a supermassive black hole in deep space

beats.text: At the center of galaxy A2261-BCG, astronomers expected a monster up to 100 billion times the mass of our Sun.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope optical image of giant galaxy A2261-BCG

beats.text: Instead, Hubble observations showed a bloated core measuring 10,000 light-years across with no concentrated peak of starlight.
beats.visual: Hubble close-up image showing the unusually diffuse starlight core of galaxy A2261-BCG

beats.text: Deep Chandra X-ray searches from 1999 and 2004 detected no signs of superheated material falling into a central black hole.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray Observatory composite image of galaxy cluster Abell 2261

beats.text: In 2018, a team led by Kayhan Gultekin of the University of Michigan tried again but also failed to find anything.
beats.visual: portrait of astrophysicist Kayhan Gultekin at the University of Michigan

beats.text: The leading theory is that asymmetric gravitational waves from a giant cosmic merger kicked the black hole completely out of the galaxy.
beats.visual: artist's illustration of a recoiling supermassive black hole ejected by gravitational waves

beats.text: Today, astronomers are still searching deep space to find this invisible, runaway giant.
beats.visual: artist concept of the James Webb Space Telescope in deep space
queries: James Webb Space Telescope space illustration

better_than_last: Applied a high-urgency curiosity-gap mystery hook in the first beat to maximize early retention, while maintaining a smooth and seamless loop at the end.
